title: chore(lint): Disallow `var` in favor of `let` and `const`

comments.body: @algolia/javascript That's now official the instantsearch.js project is using `let` as the new `var`. For good or worse we do not know :D
Let's not forget about `const` as well, we can (and should) use it.

> Let's not forget about const as well, we can (and should) use it.

https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/widgets/search-box/search-box.js#L8 :)
That was the first const, constgrats
may I ask what's the rationale behind not using var at all? ^^
I dont have an answer for this. Yet we can mix var and let but I am not sure of the value.
@olance I think the main reason is hoisting.
`let` is not hoisted to the top of the function. Meaning you can now safely have `let` variables scoped inside `if` and `while` without any collision risk with a variable defined in a higher scope.
OK, so it's a way to safeguard us from possible errors when using `var` in an inappropriate way?
Yes, it's just a `var` that works as someone discovering JavaScript would expect.
